title: Let the Right One In
synopsis: A bullied boy in a Stockholm suburb, a girl who only comes out at night, a pool, and an invitation that has to be spoken aloud.

nodes.text: Practice stabbing a tree at midnight in your underwear.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Practice” back. Lonely shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Wise.

nodes.text: A pale girl, barefoot in the snow, who tells you she cannot be your friend.

choices.consequence: “Speak to her” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Brave.
There is no taking “Walk past” back. Wise shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Conny grabs your ear at the edge of the pool with a switch.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Fight back.” The story records the instinct as “Brave” and carries it forward.
You commit to “Endure.” The story records the instinct as “Tired” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: An old man hangs a child upside down in a forest with a funnel.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honest—follows you into whatever comes next.

Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You and the box ride south for days, and the small tapping never stops, and the snow goes from white to gray to slush as the train carries you somewhere kinder.
You climb out of the pool and Eli pulls a towel around you, and the two of you walk past a half-dozen severed surprises with an even smaller smile.
Decades later you write your mother a postcard from a city she cannot name, and you sign it with a small symbol Eli taught you that means thank you for the invitation.
